Batch UI audits and side-by-side device comparison are now included in EditorCraft Device Simulator Tools.

Supports Unity **2022.3.62f2 (2022 LTS)** and **6000.6.5f1 (Unity 6)**.

## New features

- **Batch UI / Safe Area audit:** check an active scene UI root across filtered favorite devices and each profile's recorded orientations. Report screen and safe-area overflow as left/top/right/bottom pixel distances.
- **Configurable scope:** inspect UI Graphics and Selectables, optionally include layout containers, exclude entire subtrees, and set a pixel tolerance. Unsupported objects are reported as skipped.
- **Navigate from a finding:** open the captured device/orientation and select the affected scene object.
- **Native comparison gallery:** compare up to four captured screens side by side, filter by orientation, and page through larger batches using bounded thumbnails.
- **Export results:** save HTML/JSON reports, full-resolution PNGs and thumbnails. Cancellation and failures retain completed results and restore the original device/orientation when available.

The new workflow reuses the existing capture/device infrastructure. The single-object inspector shares the same projected-bound checks; existing clean/framed PNG and favorite HTML exports remain available. README and showcase now include a real Unity gallery screenshot and an eight-snapshot sample report.

## Use

Open **Device Simulator → Control Panel → EditorCraft Device Tools → Test Tools** and choose **Batch UI audit & comparison…** or **Comparison gallery…**.

[Workflow and limitations](https://github.com/dghn/editorcraft-device-simulator-tools/blob/v0.3.0/Documentation~/UI_AUDIT.md)

## Install or update

In Unity Package Manager, install from Git URL or update the existing Git dependency to:

```text
https://github.com/dghn/editorcraft-device-simulator-tools.git#v0.3.0
```

The one-command installer also defaults to v0.3.0. The package remains Editor-only; no scene-layout changes or runtime components are required.

## Validation and limits

The integration probe passed in both supported Editors: two devices × four orientations, overflow distances, scaled UI, exclusions, hidden/inactive UI, export, object navigation, cancellation, restoration, window teardown, callback failure and legacy capture regression. The play-mode transition handler was tested directly, without entering Play mode. The native Unity 6 gallery was visually inspected. Package integrity and all seven installer tests pass.

Audits compare projected RectTransform bounds; they do not assess clipping, occlusion, text readability or physical hardware. Captures are sequential while the application runs. Safe-area accuracy depends on the selected profile. Other Editor patches require validation. The existing Unity 6 deprecated dropdown-overload warning remains. Earlier clean Git-install reports are historical; this release does not claim a fresh clean-install test of this tag.
